He required that they should keep his laws. They realised that they 
were good laws. Sadly, the people found that they were unable to 
keep his commands. The old covenant was consistently broken. 
God promised that one day he would make a new covenant 
with his people. This covenant would be different from the first 
covenant: ‘I will put my law in their minds and write it on their 
hearts’ (Jeremiah 31:33). In other words, under the new covenant the 
law would be internal rather than external. If you go on a long hike, 
you start off by carrying your provisions on your back. They weigh 
you down and slow you up. But when you have eaten them, not only 
has the weight gone but you also have a new energy coming from 
inside. What God promised through Jeremiah was a time when the 
law would no longer be a weight on the outside but would become a 
source of energy from inside. But how was all this going to happen? 
Ezekiel gives us the answer. He was a prophet, and God spoke 
through him, elaborating on the earlier promise: ‘I will give you a 
new heart and put a new spirit in you,’ he said. ‘I will remove from 
you your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh. And I will put 
my Spirit in you and move you to follow my decrees and be careful 
to keep my laws’ (Ezekiel 36:26–27). 
Through the prophet Ezekiel, God was saying that this is what 
will happen when he puts his Spirit within us. This is how he will 
change our hearts and make them soft (‘hearts of flesh’) rather than 
hard (‘hearts of stone’). The Spirit of God will move us to follow his 
decrees and keep his laws. 
Jackie Pullinger has spent over thirty years working in what was 
the lawless walled city of Kowloon, Hong Kong. She has given her 
life to working with prostitutes, heroin addicts and gang members.
